subject.name: unknown_subject
subject.definition: A recent (2023–2026) open-access or abstract-visible scientific paper on large language model agents or tool-using LLM agents, with extracted title, authors, year/venue, one-sentence main claim, and URL

decisions.question: Which specific paper (title + URL) satisfies all constraints?
Is the paper open-access or only abstract-visible?
Does the publication year fall within 2023–2026?
Is the paper about LLM agents or tool-using LLM agents?
Can a one-sentence main claim or conclusion be extracted from the abstract or intro?
Are title, authors, year/venue, and URL all present in the output?

missing_to_solve: Identify a concrete paper title and URL that satisfies all constraints
Verify the paper is open-access or at least has a visible abstract (no paywall blocking)
Confirm the paper's topic is specifically about LLM agents or tool-using LLM agents
Extract a faithful one-sentence main claim or conclusion from the abstract or introduction
Record authors if visible; note if not available
Record venue (conference, journal, or preprint server) if shown
Note explicitly what was not verified (e.g., full-text claims, reproducibility, peer-review status)
contract.freeze_rationale: The contract clearly defines the subject (a specific 2023–2026 LLM-agent paper with extractable metadata), all six decisions include UNKNOWN as an outcome, sufficiency.required names every decision that must be proven (subject_instance, access_status, recency, topic_match, claim_extraction, citation_completeness), and missing_to_solve lists only runtime discoveries (finding the paper, verifying access, extracting the claim, noting unverified items) rather than structural omissions. The task's output requirement of 'citation-style line + URL + claimed finding + what was not verified' is fully covered by the observables and the citation_completeness decision (which permits PARTIAL, matching the task's 'if visible' / 'if shown' language). No structural gaps remain.
